penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: Expert-curated frontend education content requires ongoing human expert authorship — the very thing the buyer is paying for. Claude can assist but cannot replace the expert credibility signal the market explicitly demands.

penalties_applied.name: high_touch_support
penalties_applied.reason: Course/content products typically attract questions, corrections, and community interaction that require human judgment to maintain credibility.

rationale: The buyer is an individual developer paying out of pocket (~$50-200 range for a course or book), which is a real but low-value, high-churn consumer segment. The core problem — 'LLMs are insufficient, I want a human expert' — is a direct contradiction of what this factory can autonomously produce: Claude-generated content will not satisfy buyers who are explicitly rejecting AI-generated material. Operational autonomy is critically low because the product's value proposition depends on ongoing human expert authorship.
solution_plan: This opportunity is not viable for this factory. The buyer explicitly wants human expert knowledge over LLM output, which means the factory's core advantage (Claude-generated content at scale) becomes a liability rather than an asset. A solo non-technical operator could not credibly author opinionated expert frontend content at the quality level that would differentiate from free LLM outputs. Recommend dropping and watching for a signal where AI-assisted content is acceptable to the buyer.
notes: Fails operational_autonomy gate (score 3, min 7) and buildability_with_ai gate (score 4, min 6). The product's value proposition is structurally opposed to AI automation.
